q1.q: How many surahs does the Noble Qur'an consist of?
q1.exp: The Noble Qur'an consists of 114 surahs.

q2.q: Which is the longest surah of the Qur'an?
q2.exp: Surah Al-Baqara is the longest with 286 verses.

q3.q: Which is the shortest surah of the Qur'an?
q3.exp: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest with 3 verses.

q4.q: How many juz does the Qur'an consist of?
q4.exp: The Noble Qur'an consists of 30 juz.

q5.q: In which surah are the first revealed verses of the Qur'an?
q5.exp: The first revealed verses are the first 5 verses of Surah Al-'Alaq.

q6.q: How many verses does Surah Al-Fatiha consist of?
q6.exp: Surah Al-Fatiha consists of 7 verses and is also known as 'Sabʿ al-Mathani'.

q7.q: Surah Ya-Sin is which number in the Qur'an?
q7.exp: Surah Ya-Sin is the 36th surah of the Qur'an.

q8.q: How many verses are there in the Qur'an?
q8.exp: According to the generally accepted count, there are 6236 verses in the Noble Qur'an.

q9.q: Who is the only woman mentioned by name in the Qur'an?
q9.exp: The only woman mentioned by name in the Qur'an is Maryam (Mary).

q10.q: In which surah is 'Ayat al-Kursi' found?
q10.exp: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqara.

q11.q: 'Ar-Rahman' is the name of which surah number?
q11.exp: Surah Ar-Rahman is the 55th surah of the Qur'an.

q12.q: Which is the last revealed surah of the Qur'an?
q12.exp: Although scholars differ, Surah Al-Ma'ida is among the last revealed surahs.

q13.q: In which month did the revelation of the Qur'an begin?
q13.exp: The Qur'an began to be revealed in the month of Ramadan, on the Night of Power.

q14.q: Whose story is repeated most often in the Qur'an?
q14.exp: The story of Prophet Musa is the most frequently repeated prophetic narrative in the Qur'an.

q15.q: What subject does Surah Al-Ikhlas address?
q15.exp: Surah Al-Ikhlas describes the oneness of Allah (tawhid).

q16.q: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Qur'an?
q16.exp: The names of 25 prophets are mentioned in the Qur'an.

q17.q: About whom was Surah Al-Masad (Tabbat) revealed?
q17.exp: Surah Al-Masad was revealed about Abu Lahab and his wife.

q18.q: Which event is called the 'Great Victory' in the Qur'an?
q18.exp: Surah Al-Fath describes the Treaty of Hudaybiyya as 'a clear victory'.

q19.q: Surah An-Nas teaches seeking refuge from what?
o: The evil of those who whisper
q19.exp: Surah An-Nas teaches seeking refuge in Allah from the evil of those who whisper.

q20.q: What does 'Al-Furqan', another name of the Qur'an, mean?
o: The Criterion between truth and falsehood
q20.exp: Al-Furqan means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

q21.q: Which animal spoke in the presence of Prophet Sulayman in the Qur'an?
q21.exp: Surah An-Naml relates how an ant called out concerning Prophet Sulayman.

q22.q: What does Surah Al-'Asr swear by?
q22.exp: Surah Al-'Asr opens with an oath by time.

q23.q: Who produced the first comprehensive Turkish translation and commentary of the Qur'an?
q23.exp: The first comprehensive Turkish translation and commentary was produced by Elmalili Hamdi Yazir.

q24.q: Which event does Surah Al-Fil describe?
q24.exp: Surah Al-Fil describes Abraha's attempt to destroy the Kaʿba.

q25.q: Which name of Allah appears most often in the Qur'an?
q25.exp: The name 'Allah' is the most frequently occurring name in the Qur'an.

q26.q: What subject does Surah An-Naba' address?
o: The Great News (the Day of Judgment)
q26.exp: Surah An-Naba' speaks of 'the great news', that is, the Day of Judgment.

q27.q: How many prostration verses are there in the Qur'an?
q27.exp: There are 14 verses of prostration (sajdat al-tilawa) in the Qur'an.

q28.q: By what other name is Surah Al-Mulk known?
q28.exp: Surah Al-Mulk is also known as 'Tabarak' and has 30 verses.

q29.q: In which surah is the story of Prophet Yusuf told?
q29.exp: The story of Prophet Yusuf is told in detail in Surah Yusuf.

q30.q: Which juz of the Qur'an contains the most surahs?
q30.exp: Juz 30 (the 'Amma juz) contains the greatest number of surahs.

q31.exp: Dhul-Qarnayn, described in Surah Al-Kahf, is portrayed as a just ruler.

q32.q: Which caliph first ordered the compilation of the Qur'an?
q32.exp: The Qur'an was first compiled into a mushaf during the caliphate of Abu Bakr.

q33.q: During which caliph's era was the Qur'an reproduced in copies?
q33.exp: The Qur'an was copied and sent to different regions during the era of Uthman.

q34.q: By which other title is Prophet 'Isa mentioned in the Qur'an?
q34.exp: Prophet 'Isa is also called 'Ruhullah' (a spirit from Allah) in the Qur'an.

q35.q: On which day is it recommended to recite Surah Al-Kahf?
q35.exp: The merit of reciting Surah Al-Kahf on Friday is established by hadith.

q36.q: How many were the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf) in the Qur'an?
q36.exp: Al-Kahf 22 says 'seven, and the eighth of them was their dog'.

q37.q: Which Companion was the scribe of revelation?
q37.exp: Zayd ibn Thabit is the most renowned scribe of revelation.

q38.q: Which surah is called 'Umm al-Kitab' in the Qur'an?
q38.exp: Surah Al-Fatiha is named 'Umm al-Kitab', the mother of the Book.

q39.q: Which two surahs are known as 'Al-Muʿawwidhatayn'?
q39.exp: Surahs Al-Falaq and An-Nas are known as 'Al-Muʿawwidhatayn', the surahs of seeking refuge.

q40.q: Which command is repeated most often in the Qur'an?
q40.exp: The call to reflect and use reason is among the most frequently repeated commands in the Qur'an.

q41.q: Surah Ta-Ha mainly recounts the story of which prophet?
q41.exp: Surah Ta-Ha largely recounts the story of Prophet Musa.

q42.q: Which surah does 'Sabʿ al-Mathani' refer to?
q42.exp: 'Sabʿ al-Mathani' (the seven oft-repeated verses) is a name given to Surah Al-Fatiha.

q43.q: Into how many groups does Surah Al-Waqi'a divide people?
q43.exp: Surah Al-Waqi'a divides people into 3 groups: the Foremost, the Companions of the Right, and the Companions of the Left.

q44.q: Which metal is mentioned in the Qur'an as a material of great might?
q44.exp: In Surah Al-Hadid, iron is described as a material of great might.

q45.q: What are the surahs revealed in Mecca called?
q45.exp: Surahs revealed during the Meccan period are called 'Meccan surahs'.

q46.q: What are the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqara known as?

q47.q: What is the officially compiled mushaf of the Qur'an called?
q47.exp: The mushaf reproduced under Uthman is called the 'Uthmanic Mushaf'.

q48.q: In which period was Surah Ad-Duha revealed to the Prophet?
q48.exp: Surah Ad-Duha was revealed as consolation during a period when revelation had paused for a while.

q49.q: What is 'Al-Bayt al-Maʿmur' in the Qur'an?
o: A house of worship in the heavens
q49.exp: Al-Bayt al-Maʿmur is the house of worship in the seventh heaven circumambulated by the angels.

q50.q: Who is Luqman in the Qur'an?
q50.exp: Luqman was not a prophet but a righteous servant granted wisdom.

q51.exp: Prophet Adam is both the first human being and the first prophet.

q52.exp: Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is the final prophet, the Seal of the Prophets.

q53.q: On which mountain did Prophet Nuh's ark come to rest?
q53.exp: According to the Qur'an, the ark came to rest upon Mount Judi.

q54.q: What is the epithet of Prophet Ibrahim?
q54.exp: Prophet Ibrahim is called 'Khalilullah', the friend of Allah.

q55.q: Which pharaoh did Prophet Musa confront?
q55.exp: According to the prevailing view, Prophet Musa lived during the era of Ramesses II.

q56.q: In which land did Prophet Yusuf become a ruler?
q56.exp: Prophet Yusuf became an administrator in Egypt, serving as minister of the treasury.

q57.q: In the belly of which creature did Prophet Yunus remain?
q57.exp: Prophet Yunus remained in the belly of a great fish and was delivered after calling upon Allah.

q58.q: With which beings could Prophet Sulayman speak?
q58.exp: Prophet Sulayman was taught the speech of animals and of the jinn.

q59.q: Who was the mother of Prophet 'Isa?
q59.exp: The mother of Prophet 'Isa was Maryam.

q60.q: Which scripture was revealed to Prophet Dawud?
q60.exp: The Zabur was revealed to Prophet Dawud.

q61.q: Which scripture was revealed to Prophet Musa?
q61.exp: The Torah was revealed to Prophet Musa.

q62.q: Who was the father of Prophet Isma'il?
q62.exp: Prophet Isma'il was the son of Prophet Ibrahim.

q63.q: For which quality is Prophet Ayyub known?
q63.exp: Prophet Ayyub is renowned for the patience he showed through his illness and trials.

q64.q: At what age did Prophet Muhammad receive prophethood?
q64.exp: Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) received the mission of prophethood at the age of 40.

q65.q: For what is Prophet Idris known?
q65.exp: It is related that Prophet Idris was the first to write and the first to practise tailoring.

q66.q: What is the other name of Prophet Yaʿqub?
q66.exp: The other name of Prophet Yaʿqub is Israel; the Children of Israel descend from him.

q67.q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet?
q67.exp: Khadija was the Prophet's first wife and the first person to believe.

q68.q: Into whose fire was Prophet Ibrahim cast?
q68.exp: Prophet Ibrahim was cast into the fire by Nimrod, but Allah made the fire cool for him.

q69.q: To which people was Prophet Lut sent?
q69.exp: Prophet Lut was sent to the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.

q70.q: To which people was Prophet Salih sent?
q70.exp: Prophet Salih was sent to the people of Thamud.

q71.q: To which people was Prophet Hud sent?
q71.exp: Prophet Hud was sent to the people of 'Ad.

q72.q: To which people was Prophet Shuʿayb sent?
q72.exp: Prophet Shuʿayb was sent to the people of Madyan.

q73.q: By which miracle was Prophet 'Isa born?
q73.exp: Prophet 'Isa was born to Maryam without a father.

q74.q: What was the name of the Prophet's uncle?
q74.exp: The Prophet had several uncles; Hamza and Abbas were among those who accepted Islam.

q75.q: What was built first when the Prophet migrated to Medina?
q75.exp: On reaching Medina, the Prophet first built the Quba Mosque.

q76.q: Who was the first man to accept Islam?
q76.exp: Abu Bakr was the first among adult men to accept Islam.

q77.q: Who was the first woman to accept Islam?
q77.exp: Khadija was the first person to accept Islam.

q78.q: To whom was the title 'As-Siddiq' given?
q78.exp: Abu Bakr was given the title 'As-Siddiq', the utterly truthful.

q79.q: To whom does the title 'Al-Faruq' belong?
q79.exp: Umar was given the title 'Al-Faruq' for distinguishing truth from falsehood.

q80.q: To which caliph does the title 'Dhun-Nurayn' belong?
q80.exp: Uthman is called 'Dhun-Nurayn' (possessor of two lights); he married two daughters of the Prophet.

q81.q: Whose wife was Fatima, the daughter of the Prophet?
q81.exp: Fatima was the wife of Ali.

q82.exp: Bilal al-Habashi was the first muezzin of Islam.

q83.q: To whom does the title 'The Sword of Allah' belong?
q83.exp: Khalid ibn al-Walid was given the title 'Sayfullah', the Sword of Allah.

q84.q: What was the epithet of Hamza?
q84.exp: Hamza was given the epithet 'Asadullah', the Lion of Allah.

q85.exp: Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph after the Prophet.

q86.q: Who headed the first committee that compiled the Qur'an?
q86.exp: Zayd ibn Thabit headed the committee that compiled the Qur'an.

q87.q: Which Companion narrated the most hadiths?
q87.exp: Abu Hurayra narrated the most hadiths, some 5374.

q88.q: Which of these was an uncle of the Prophet?
q88.exp: Abu Talib, Abbas and Hamza were all uncles of the Prophet.

q89.q: Who led the first group that migrated to Abyssinia?
q89.exp: Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib was prominent in the first migration to Abyssinia.

q90.q: Where was Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet, martyred?

q91.q: In whose house did the Prophet stay as a guest in Medina?
q91.exp: On arriving in Medina, the Prophet stayed in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.

q92.exp: Umar served as caliph for 10 years (634-644).

q93.q: How many Muslims fought at the Battle of Badr?
q93.exp: The Muslims at the Battle of Badr numbered roughly 313.

q94.q: How many Companions were martyred at the Battle of Uhud?
q94.exp: Roughly 70 Companions were martyred at the Battle of Uhud.

q95.q: Who was the wet nurse of the Prophet?
q95.exp: Halima was the wet nurse of the Prophet.

q96.q: Who was the Prophet's companion during the Hijra?
q96.exp: Abu Bakr migrated with the Prophet from Mecca to Medina.

q97.q: Who proposed digging the trench at the Battle of the Trench?
q97.exp: The idea of digging a trench came from the Persian Companion Salman al-Farisi.

q98.q: What were the names of Ali's sons?
q98.exp: The sons of Ali were Hasan and Husayn.

q99.q: Which of the Prophet's daughters passed away last?
q99.exp: Fatima passed away six months after the Prophet.

q100.q: Who was the first child to enter Islam?
q100.exp: Ali was the first among children to accept Islam.

q101.q: In which year did the Hijra take place?
q101.exp: The Hijra from Mecca to Medina took place in 622.

q102.q: In which year was Istanbul conquered?
q102.exp: Istanbul was conquered in 1453 by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.

q103.q: In which year was the Battle of Badr fought?
q103.exp: The Battle of Badr was fought in the 2nd year after the Hijra.

q104.q: In which country was the Umayyad State of Andalusia founded?
q104.exp: The Umayyad State of Andalusia was founded in Spain in 756.

q105.exp: The Ottoman State was founded in 1299 by Osman Gazi.

q106.q: In which year was Mecca conquered?
q106.exp: Mecca was conquered in the 8th year after the Hijra.

q107.q: Where was the first Islamic state established?
q107.exp: The first Islamic state was established in Medina.

q108.q: What was the capital of the Umayyad State?
q108.exp: The capital of the Umayyad State was Damascus.

q109.q: What was the capital of the Abbasid State?
q109.exp: The capital of the Abbasid State was Baghdad.

q110.q: When did Baghdad fall during the Mongol invasion?
q110.exp: Baghdad was taken by Hulagu Khan in 1258.

q111.q: Which commander retook Jerusalem from the Crusaders?
q111.exp: Saladin retook Jerusalem in 1187 after the Battle of Hattin.

q112.q: In which year was the Battle of Manzikert fought?
q112.exp: The Battle of Manzikert was won in 1071 under the command of Alp Arslan.

q113.q: Which is the first Muslim university?
q113.exp: Al-Qarawiyyin University in Morocco, founded in 859, is the world's oldest university.

q114.q: In which year was the Treaty of Hudaybiyya concluded?
q114.exp: The Treaty of Hudaybiyya was concluded in the 6th year after the Hijra.

q115.q: In which year was the Farewell Sermon delivered?
q115.exp: The Farewell Sermon was delivered at Arafat in the 10th year after the Hijra.

q116.q: At what age did the Prophet pass away?
q116.exp: The Prophet passed away at the age of 63.

q117.q: In which era was the first Islamic coin minted?
q117.exp: The first Islamic coin was minted during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.

q118.q: In which year was the Battle of Gallipoli fought?
q118.exp: The Battle of Gallipoli was fought in 1915.

q119.exp: The Great Seljuk State was founded in 1040 by Tughril and Chaghri Beg.

q120.q: Which is the famous palace of Andalusia?
q120.exp: The Alhambra Palace in Granada is a masterpiece of Islamic architecture.

q121.q: Who was the last Ottoman sultan?
q121.exp: The last Ottoman sultan was Mehmed VI Vahideddin.

q122.q: During which caliph's era did Muslims first conquer Jerusalem?
q122.exp: Jerusalem was conquered in 638 during the era of Umar.

q123.q: In which year did the First Crusade begin?
q123.exp: The First Crusade began in the year 1096.

q124.q: Where did the Prophet build the Prophet's Mosque?
q124.exp: The Prophet's Mosque was built in Medina.

q125.q: Where was the first hospital in the Muslim world established?
q125.exp: The first great hospital in the Muslim world was established in Baghdad during the Abbasid era.

q126.q: How many books make up the 'Kutub al-Sitta' in hadith scholarship?
q126.exp: The Kutub al-Sitta refers to the six principal books of hadith.

q127.q: Who is the author of Sahih al-Bukhari?
q127.exp: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by Imam al-Bukhari (810-870).

q128.q: In which book is the hadith 'deeds are by intentions' found?
q128.exp: This hadith appears in many collections of hadith.

q129.q: Which caliph first encouraged the writing down of hadith?
q129.exp: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ordered the official recording of hadith.

q130.exp: A mawduʿ hadith is a fabricated hadith.

q131.q: What does 'isnad' mean in hadith scholarship?
q131.exp: The isnad is the chain of narrators who transmitted the hadith.

o: A hadith with a single narrator
A hadith transmitted by many narrators
q132.exp: A mutawatir hadith is one transmitted by a great many narrators at every level.

q133.q: In the hadith 'Islam is built upon five', what is the first pillar?
q133.exp: The first of the pillars of Islam is the testimony of faith (shahada).

q134.q: What is the source of the hadith 'Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers'?
q134.exp: This hadith is narrated in An-Nasa'i.

q135.q: What is the Prophet's final sermon called?
q135.exp: The Prophet's final sermon at Arafat is called the 'Farewell Sermon'.

q136.q: Who is the author of Sahih Muslim?
q136.exp: Sahih Muslim was compiled by Imam Muslim (821-875).

q137.q: Which book is NOT part of the Kutub al-Sitta?
q137.exp: Imam Malik's Al-Muwatta is not part of the Kutub al-Sitta.

q138.q: What is the meaning of the hadith 'Make things easy, do not make them difficult'?
q138.exp: The Prophet commanded that ease be shown to people in matters of religion.

q139.q: What does 'matn' mean in hadith scholarship?
q139.exp: The matn is the content or wording of the hadith; the isnad is the chain of narrators.

o: A word from Allah not found in the Qur'an
q140.exp: A hadith qudsi is one whose meaning is from Allah and whose wording is from the Prophet.

q141.q: What is the source of the hadith 'A smile is charity'?
q141.exp: This hadith is narrated in At-Tirmidhi.

q142.q: What does 'sahih' mean in hadith scholarship?
q142.exp: A sahih hadith is a reliable hadith meeting all the required conditions.

q143.q: How does the hadith 'A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim' continue?
q143.exp: It continues: he does not wrong him, abandon him, or despise him.

q144.q: What kind of report is the saying 'Seek knowledge even in China'?
q144.exp: This saying has been graded weak by hadith scholars.

q145.q: Which food did the Prophet love most?
q145.exp: It is narrated in hadith that the Prophet greatly loved dishes made with gourd.

q146.exp: A hasan hadith is of middling grade, between sahih and weak.

q147.q: What are the hadiths describing the Prophet's daily life called?
q147.exp: Hadiths describing the Prophet's physical and moral qualities are called 'Shamail'.

q148.q: How does the hadith 'Whoever sees an evil, let him change it with his hand' continue?
o: If he cannot, with his tongue
If he cannot, with his heart
q148.exp: Let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, with his tongue; if he cannot, let him detest it in his heart.

q149.q: Which colour did the Prophet love?
q149.exp: The Prophet loved the colour white and wore white garments.

q150.q: Who narrated the hadith 'Convey from me, even a single verse'?
q150.exp: This hadith was narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr.

q151.q: How many obligatory prayers are there each day?
q151.exp: In Islam, five daily prayers are obligatory.

q152.q: How many rakʿas is the Fajr prayer?
q152.exp: The obligatory part of the Fajr prayer is 2 rakʿas.

q153.q: How many obligatory rakʿas is the Dhuhr prayer?
q153.exp: The obligatory part of the Dhuhr prayer is 4 rakʿas.

q154.q: Which of these does NOT invalidate wudu?

q155.q: How many rakʿas is the Friday prayer?
q155.exp: The obligatory part of the Friday prayer is 2 rakʿas.

q156.q: At which event was the prayer made obligatory?
q156.exp: The prayer was made obligatory on the night of the Miʿraj.

q157.q: Which surah is recited first in the prayer?
q157.exp: Reciting Surah Al-Fatiha in every rakʿa is obligatory.

q158.q: Which glorification is said in prostration?

q159.q: Which glorification is said in bowing (rukuʿ)?

q160.q: Which of these is NOT a pillar of the prayer?
q160.exp: The qunut supplication is not a pillar of the prayer but a recommended supplication in certain prayers.

q161.q: At which time is the Witr prayer performed?
q161.exp: The Witr prayer is performed after the Isha prayer.

q162.q: While travelling, how many rakʿas are the four-rakʿa obligatory prayers prayed?
q162.exp: While travelling, four-rakʿa obligatory prayers are shortened to 2 rakʿas.

q163.q: How many takbirs are said in the funeral prayer?
q163.exp: Four takbirs are said in the funeral prayer.

q164.q: In which part of the prayer is the tashahhud recited?
q164.exp: The tashahhud (at-tahiyyat) is recited in the final sitting.

q165.q: What is the juristic term for facing the qibla in prayer?
q165.exp: Facing the qibla is called 'istiqbal al-qibla'.

q166.q: How many extra takbirs are said in the Eid prayer?
q166.exp: A total of 6 extra takbirs are said across the two rakʿas of the Eid prayer.

q167.exp: Tayammum is performed when water is unavailable or cannot be used.

q168.q: Which of these invalidates the prayer?
q168.exp: Speaking deliberately during the prayer invalidates it.

q169.q: How many obligatory rakʿas is the Asr prayer?
q169.exp: The obligatory part of the Asr prayer is 4 rakʿas.

q170.q: How many obligatory rakʿas is the Maghrib prayer?
q170.exp: The obligatory part of the Maghrib prayer is 3 rakʿas.

q171.q: What is the first sitting in the prayer called?
q171.exp: The first sitting is called 'qaʿda al-ula'.

q172.q: When is the 'prostration of forgetfulness' performed in prayer?
q172.exp: The prostration of forgetfulness is performed when a mistake occurs in the prayer.

q173.q: Which of these is a recommended (mustahabb) prayer?
q173.exp: The Duha (forenoon) prayer is among the recommended prayers.

q174.q: Before the Kaʿba, in which direction was the prayer offered?
q174.exp: The first qibla was Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.

q175.q: When was the qibla changed from Al-Aqsa to the Kaʿba?
q175.exp: The qibla was turned toward the Kaʿba in the 2nd year of the Hijra.

q176.q: In which Hijri year was fasting in Ramadan made obligatory?
q176.exp: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in the 2nd year of the Hijra.

q177.q: In which surah is the Night of Power mentioned?
q177.exp: The Night of Power is described in Surah Al-Qadr.

q178.q: How many days does Eid al-Fitr last?

q179.q: In which month is the Tarawih prayer performed?
q179.exp: Tarawih is a sunna prayer performed during the month of Ramadan.

q180.q: When should the fitra charity be given?
q180.exp: The fitra should be given before the Eid prayer.

q181.q: Which act that breaks the fast requires making it up?
q181.exp: Eating or drinking deliberately breaks the fast and requires making it up.

o: Staying in the mosque for worship
q182.exp: Iʿtikaf is staying in the mosque with the intention of worship.

q183.q: Until when may the pre-dawn meal be eaten?
q183.exp: The pre-dawn meal may be eaten until the time of imsak (true dawn).

q184.q: What is required of those unable to fast?
q184.exp: Those unable to fast due to chronic illness and similar reasons give fidya.

q185.q: The Night of Power is equivalent to how much?
q185.exp: Surah Al-Qadr says it is 'better than a thousand months'. A thousand months is about 83 years.

q186.q: Ramadan is which month of the Hijri calendar?
q186.exp: Ramadan is the 9th month of the Hijri calendar.

q187.q: Is it permissible to use the miswak while fasting?
q187.exp: Using the miswak is permissible while fasting.

q188.q: Performing umra in Ramadan is equal in reward to what?
q188.exp: The Prophet said that umra performed in Ramadan equals a Hajj.

q189.q: What is the expiation (kaffara) for breaking a fast?
q189.exp: The expiation is fasting 60 consecutive days or feeding 60 poor people.

q190.q: Which act of worship is especially performed in the last ten days of Ramadan?
q190.exp: Entering iʿtikaf during the last ten days of Ramadan is a sunna.

q191.q: With which supplication is the fast broken?
q191.exp: 'Allahumma laka sumtu wa bika amantu wa alayka tawakkaltu wa ala rizqika aftartu'

q192.q: May pregnant and nursing women fast?
o: They may abstain and make it up later
q192.exp: If there is concern for health, they may abstain and make the fast up later.

q193.q: Which are the three sacred months?
q193.exp: The three blessed months are Rajab, Shaʿban and Ramadan.

q194.q: In which month is the Night of Baraʾa observed?
q194.exp: The Night of Baraʾa is the 15th night of the month of Shaʿban.

q195.q: When is the time of iftar?
o: The time of the Maghrib prayer
q195.exp: Iftar is taken at sunset, with the Maghrib call to prayer.

q196.q: How many are the pillars of Islam?
q196.exp: The pillars of Islam are 5: the testimony of faith, prayer, fasting, zakat and Hajj.

q197.q: How many are the articles of faith?

q198.q: What is the zakat threshold (nisab) for gold?
q198.exp: The zakat threshold for gold is 20 mithqal (about 80.18 grams).

q199.q: In which month is the Hajj performed?
q199.exp: The Hajj is performed in the month of Dhul-Hijja.

q200.q: How many days does Eid al-Adha last?

q201.q: Which of these is one of the four great school founders?
q201.exp: The four great schools are Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali.

q202.exp: The Hanafi school was founded by Imam al-Aʿzam Abu Hanifa.

q203.q: What percentage of wealth is zakat?
q203.exp: Zakat is one-fortieth of wealth, that is 2.5%.

q204.q: How many times in a lifetime is Hajj obligatory?
q204.exp: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for every Muslim who is able.

q205.q: How many circuits around the Kaʿba make up the tawaf?
q205.exp: The tawaf consists of circling the Kaʿba 7 times.

q206.exp: Saʿy is walking 7 times between the hills of Safa and Marwa.

q207.q: When is the ʿaqiqa sacrifice offered?
q207.exp: The ʿaqiqa is a sacrifice offered when a child is born, on the 7th day.

q208.q: How many are the obligatory acts of the ritual bath (ghusl)?
q208.exp: The obligatory acts of ghusl are 3: rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose, and washing the whole body.

q209.exp: Ihram is the seamless garment worn for Hajj or umra.

q210.q: In inheritance law, a woman's share is how much of a man's?
q210.exp: As a general rule a woman's share is half that of a man, though there are exceptions.

q211.q: Which is a condition of the marriage contract?
q211.exp: The conditions of marriage are offer and acceptance, witnesses, the dower, and the guardian's consent.

q212.q: To whom may zakat NOT be given?
q212.exp: Zakat may not be given to one's ascendants (parents) or descendants (children).

q213.q: For what purpose is the istikhara prayer performed?
o: To seek guidance toward what is best
q213.exp: The istikhara prayer is performed to ask Allah for what is best in a matter.

q214.q: At minimum, how much of the Qur'an must be recited in the prayer?
q214.exp: According to the Hanafi school, at least 3 short verses or 1 long verse should be recited after Al-Fatiha.

q215.q: Which act of worship is prohibited for women during menstruation?
q215.exp: Performing the prayer and fasting are prohibited during menstruation.

q216.q: Which Muslim scholar is considered the founder of algebra?
q216.exp: Al-Khwarizmi (780-850) is considered the founder of algebra.

q217.q: In which field is Ibn Sina renowned?
q217.exp: Ibn Sina (980-1037) is renowned in medicine for his work 'The Canon of Medicine'.

q218.q: Which Muslim scholar pioneered the science of optics?
q218.exp: Ibn al-Haytham (965-1040) is regarded as the pioneer of optics.

q219.q: Who is regarded as the first Muslim chemist?
q219.exp: Jabir ibn Hayyan (721-815) is regarded as the father of modern chemistry.

q220.exp: The architect Sinan built the Selimiye Mosque as his masterwork.

q221.q: In which city is the Suleymaniye Mosque?
q221.exp: The Suleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul is a work of the architect Sinan.

q222.q: What was the 'House of Wisdom' in Islamic civilization?
q222.exp: The House of Wisdom was the great centre of learning and translation in Baghdad.

q223.q: Ibn Khaldun is considered the founder of which discipline?
q223.exp: Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406) is the founder of sociology and the philosophy of history.

q224.exp: The Muʿallaqat al-Sabʿ are 7 celebrated Arabic odes from the pre-Islamic period.

q225.q: What does 'kulliye' mean in Turkish-Islamic architecture?
o: A complex of buildings centred on a mosque
q225.exp: A kulliye includes a madrasa, bathhouse, soup kitchen and other buildings around a mosque.

q226.q: Who established the first Islamic hospital?
q226.exp: The first Islamic hospital was established during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Walid ibn Abd al-Malik.

q227.q: By which epithet is Al-Farabi known?
q227.exp: Al-Farabi was given the epithet 'al-Muʿallim al-Thani', the Second Teacher.

q228.q: Which script is most widely used in the art of calligraphy?
q228.exp: The Naskh script is the most widely used style for writing the Qur'an.

q229.q: For what is Ibn Battuta renowned?
q229.exp: Ibn Battuta (1304-1369) is the famed traveller who journeyed some 75,000 miles.

q230.q: Which is Al-Ghazali's most famous work?
q230.exp: Imam al-Ghazali's most famous work is 'Ihya 'Ulum al-Din'.

q231.q: In which city did Mawlana Jalal ad-Din Rumi live?
q231.exp: Rumi lived in Konya and wrote the Mathnawi there.

q232.q: Which is the architect Sinan's apprentice work?
q232.exp: The Sehzade Mosque is the apprentice work of the architect Sinan.

q233.q: For roughly how many centuries did Muslims remain in Andalusia?
q233.exp: Muslims remained in Andalusia for roughly 800 years (711-1492).

q234.q: In which field is Al-Biruni considered a pioneer?
q234.exp: Al-Biruni (973-1048) was a pioneer in geography, astronomy and geodesy.

q235.q: Where was the first paper mill in the Muslim world established?
q235.exp: The first Islamic paper mill was established in Samarkand in the 8th century.

q236.q: What is the qibla of the Muslims?
q236.exp: The qibla of the Muslims is the Kaʿba in Mecca.

q237.q: In which year was Prophet Muhammad born?
q237.exp: Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was born in Mecca in 571 (the Year of the Elephant).

q238.q: What is the holiest place in Islam?
q238.exp: The Kaʿba is the holiest place in Islam.

q239.q: Which country has the largest Muslim population?
q239.exp: Indonesia is the most populous Muslim country with over 230 million Muslims.

q240.q: With which event does the Hijri calendar begin?
q240.exp: The Hijri calendar begins with the Prophet's migration to Medina.

q241.exp: 'La ilaha illallah Muhammadur Rasulullah' is the fundamental statement of Islamic belief.

q242.q: Which drink is forbidden in Islam?
q242.exp: Alcohol is strictly forbidden in Islam.

q243.q: On which day is the standing at Arafat performed?
q243.exp: The standing at Arafat takes place on the 9th of Dhul-Hijja, the Day of Arafa.

q244.q: In which city was Prophet Muhammad born?
q244.exp: Prophet Muhammad was born in Mecca.

q245.q: Where was the first call to prayer given in Islam?
q245.exp: The first adhan was given in Medina by Bilal.

q246.q: Where in the prayer is the Subhanaka supplication recited?
q246.exp: Subhanaka is recited after the opening takbir.

q247.exp: As-Sirat is the bridge over Hellfire.

q248.q: What does belief in the angels require in Islam?
q248.exp: Belief in angels means believing in their existence.

q249.q: Who are the four great angels?
q249.exp: The four great angels are Jibril, Mikail, Israfil and Azrail.

q250.q: What is the duty of Israfil?
q250.exp: Israfil is the angel who will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgment.

q251.q: How many Meccan surahs are there in the Qur'an?
q251.exp: 86 surahs were revealed in Mecca and 28 in Medina.

q252.q: Which was the first complete surah revealed?
q252.exp: Surah Al-Fatiha is the first complete surah revealed, according to some views.

q253.q: Who was the foster sister of Prophet Muhammad?
q253.exp: Shayma, the daughter of Halima, was the Prophet's foster sister.

q254.q: Which caliph was a son-in-law of the Prophet?
q254.exp: Uthman (Ruqayya and Umm Kulthum) and Ali (Fatima) were sons-in-law of the Prophet.

q255.q: Which Muslim commander fought the first naval battle?
q255.exp: The first Islamic naval battle was fought by Muʿawiya during the era of Uthman.

q256.q: In which book does the hadith 'Purity is half of faith' appear?
q256.exp: This hadith appears in Sahih Muslim.

q257.q: How many distinct phrases does the adhan contain?
q257.exp: The adhan contains 7 distinct phrases, some of which are repeated.

q258.q: What does 'fatwa' mean in Islamic law?
q258.exp: A fatwa is a scholar's considered opinion on a religious matter.

q259.q: In which field is Ibn Rushd renowned?
q259.exp: Ibn Rushd (1126-1198) is renowned in philosophy and Islamic law.

q260.exp: The Miʿraj is the Prophet's ascension to the heavens.

q262.q: Which fruit is mentioned as a fruit of Paradise in the Qur'an?
q262.exp: The Qur'an mentions grapes, dates, pomegranates and olives among the blessings of Paradise.

q263.q: Why was Prophet Adam removed from the Garden?
q263.exp: Prophet Adam and his wife were removed from the Garden for approaching the forbidden tree.

q264.q: Who was the first martyr of Islam?
q264.exp: Sumayya was the first woman martyr of Islam.

q265.exp: Granada, the last Islamic state in Andalusia, fell in 1492.

q266.q: How many meals a day did the Prophet eat?
q266.exp: The Prophet generally ate two meals a day, morning and evening.

q267.q: When is the Tahajjud prayer performed?
o: After the middle of the night
q267.exp: Tahajjud is a voluntary prayer performed after waking during the night.

q268.q: What is the tradition of reciting the whole Qur'an together in Ramadan called?
q268.exp: Mukabala is the tradition of reciting the Qur'an together in Ramadan.

q269.exp: Sadaqa jariya is charity of lasting benefit, such as a fountain or a mosque.

q270.q: What is the name of Ibn Sina's book on medicine?
q270.exp: The Canon of Medicine was used as a medical textbook in Europe for centuries.

o: There is no god but Allah
q271.exp: Bismillah means 'in the name of Allah'.

q272.exp: Shirk is associating partners with Allah and is the gravest sin.

q273.q: What is the covering of the Kaʿba called?
q273.exp: The black covering of the Kaʿba is called the 'Kiswa'.

q274.q: How many people were saved aboard Prophet Nuh's ark according to the Qur'an?
q274.exp: The Qur'an does not state an exact number of those aboard Prophet Nuh's ark.

q275.exp: Prophet Isma'il and his mother Hajar lived in Mecca.

q276.q: Where is the Mosque of the Two Qiblas?
q276.exp: Masjid al-Qiblatayn (the mosque of the two qiblas) is in Medina.

q277.q: In which year was the Abbasid State founded?
q277.exp: The Abbasid State was founded in the year 750.

q278.q: What does the hadith 'None of you should sleep full while his neighbour is hungry' emphasise?
q278.exp: This hadith emphasises Islam's principle of social solidarity and justice.

q279.q: What does 'qawma' mean in the prayer?
q279.exp: Qawma is rising from the bowing and standing upright.

q280.q: When must the intention to fast be made?
q280.exp: The intention to fast must be made during the night, before the time of imsak.

q281.q: What is the ruling on riba (interest) in Islam?
q281.exp: Interest is strictly forbidden in Islam.

q282.q: During which sultan's reign was Topkapi Palace built?
q282.exp: Topkapi Palace was built by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.

o: Turning back from sin toward Allah
q283.exp: Tawba is regretting sin and turning back to Allah.

q284.q: Which Companion is mentioned by name in the Qur'an?
q284.exp: The only Companion mentioned by name in the Qur'an is Zayd ibn Haritha.

q285.q: Which miracle did the staff of Prophet Musa display?
q285.exp: The staff of Prophet Musa displayed miracles such as turning into a serpent, parting the sea and bringing water from a rock.

q286.q: Who delivered the first Friday sermon?
q286.exp: According to one report, the first Friday sermon in Medina was delivered by Asʿad ibn Zurara.

q287.q: In which year did the Ottoman State come to an end?
q287.exp: The Ottoman sultanate was abolished in 1922.

o: There is no god but Allah
q288.exp: Alhamdulillah means 'all praise belongs to Allah'.

q289.q: Upon whom is the funeral prayer obligatory in Islam?
q289.exp: The funeral prayer is a communal obligation; if a group performs it, the rest are absolved.

q290.q: What is the Prophet's mosque in Medina called?
q290.exp: The Prophet's mosque in Medina is called Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

q291.q: What does 'al-ʿArsh' mean in the Qur'an?
q291.exp: Al-ʿArsh is described as the exalted Throne of Allah.

q292.q: For how many years did Prophet Nuh call his people?
q292.exp: According to the Qur'an, Prophet Nuh called his people for 950 years.

q293.q: How long was Abu Bakr's caliphate?
q293.exp: Abu Bakr served as caliph for roughly 2 years (632-634).

q294.exp: Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed at Gibraltar and conquered Spain in 711.

q295.q: What does 'taʿdil al-arkan' mean in the prayer?
q295.exp: Taʿdil al-arkan is performing every pillar of the prayer calmly and properly.

q296.q: From which metals were the first Islamic coins made?
q296.exp: The first Islamic coins were minted in gold (dinar) and silver (dirham).

q297.q: Which Companion did the Prophet love most?
q297.exp: The Prophet described Abu Bakr as the friend he loved most.

q298.q: What is a person who has memorised the whole Qur'an called?
q298.exp: A person who has memorised the Qur'an from beginning to end is called a 'Hafiz'.

q299.exp: Allahu Akbar means 'Allah is the greatest'.

o: The place of gathering on the Day of Judgment
q300.exp: Mahshar is the place where all people will be gathered on the Day of Judgment.
